problems.title: Count distinct roots of a product
problems.question: How many roots of cos3x sin4x=0 lie in (π/2,3π/2)?
problems.idea: Solve each factor and avoid counting shared roots twice.
formulas: cos3x=0 gives x=π/6+kπ/3; sin4x=0 gives x=kπ/4.
steps: The first factor contributes 5π/6,7π/6.
The second contributes 3π/4,π,5π/4.
These five points are distinct; both interval endpoints are excluded.

problems.title: Midpoint section of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: All edges of SABC are equal. Compare base ABC with the section through the midpoints of AB,AC,AS.
problems.idea: The section is a half-scale copy of face BCS.
steps: Every face has the same area.
The section has one quarter of a face’s area, so base/section=4.

problems.title: Limit the cosine argument first
problems.question: Count the roots of 2cos(π√(1-x²))=-1.
problems.idea: The square root restricts the cosine argument to [0,π].
steps: Squaring gives x²=5/9, hence x=±√5/3.
Both satisfy the original domain.

problems.title: Product to sum leaves a constant
problems.question: Evaluate 2sin43°sin17°-cos26°.
problems.idea: Use the difference and sum of the two angles.
steps: The cos26° terms cancel.
The result is -cos60°=-1/2.

problems.title: Two shifted functions are identical
problems.question: Find all m for which cos(x+109°)=sin(x+199°)-m has a solution.
problems.idea: The phase difference is 90°.
steps: The equation reduces to 0=-m.
For m=0 every x works; otherwise no x works.

problems.title: Test an angle in the listed equations
problems.question: Which listed equation is satisfied by x=195°?
problems.idea: Reduce 4x and 3x.
steps: sin4x=√3/2, while cos4x=1/2.
At 3x, sine and cosine are both -√2/2.
Only sin4x=√3/2 matches the listed equations.

problems.title: Find every side of the cube section
problems.question: A cube has edge 6. M is the midpoint of CC₁ and N of AD. Find the shortest side of the section through B₁,N,M.
problems.idea: Use a unit cube and intersect its edges with the section plane.
steps: Their side lengths in a unit cube are √13/6,5/6,√5/2,5/4,√5/4.
The least is √5/4. Multiply by the edge 6 to obtain 3√5/2.

problems.title: Use the principal inverse-angle ranges
problems.question: Evaluate arcsin(-1/2)-arccos(-√3/2)+arctan(-√3)+arccot(-1).
problems.idea: Use the usual arccot range (0,π).
steps: The four angles are -π/6,5π/6,-π/3,3π/4.
Their signed sum is -π/6-5π/6-π/3+3π/4=-7π/12.
problems.note: Arccot is taken in (0,π), the convention used by the printed choices.

problems.title: Line-to-plane angle in a dihedral angle
problems.question: AB lies in one face of a dihedral angle β and makes angle α with its edge at A. Find the sine of its angle to the other face.
problems.idea: Resolve AB perpendicular to the shared edge, then perpendicular to the other face.
steps: The component normal to the edge has length AB sinα.
Its component normal to the second face is AB sinα sinβ.
Divide by AB.

problems.title: Amplitude of a cosine difference
problems.question: Find the minimum of cos(x+70°)-cos(x+10°).
problems.idea: Apply the cosine difference identity.
steps: The expression is -2sin(x+40°)sin30°=-sin(x+40°).
Its minimum is -1.

problems.title: Both branches of a sine equation
problems.question: Solve sinx=sin20°.
problems.idea: Equal sines occur at equal angles or supplementary angles modulo 360°.
steps: With α=20°, the second branch is 160°+360°k.

problems.title: Check whether a section reaches the top face
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 16 and height 10√6. A plane through AB makes 60° with the base and cuts the prism. What shape is the section?
problems.idea: Compare its height over C with the prism height.
steps: Since 24<10√6, the plane meets the vertical edge through C before the top face.
Thus the section has vertices A,B and a point on CC₁.
Symmetry about the perpendicular bisector of AB makes its two sloping sides equal. It is not equilateral: those sides are 8√13, while AB=16.

problems.title: Edges and space diagonals of a prism
problems.question: Which listed total 24,30,27,21,40,36 can be the number of edges plus diagonals of a prism?
problems.idea: Use n for the number of sides of its base.
steps: A space diagonal joins vertices on different bases that do not share a face.
Only 36 is a square of an integer n≥3 among the choices.
It occurs for a hexagonal prism, n=6.
problems.note: Here “diagonal” means a space diagonal of the prism, excluding face diagonals. Counting every vertex-pair diagonal would use a different convention.

problems.title: Every cause of an undefined denominator
problems.question: Where is y=1/(tanx-sinx) undefined?
problems.idea: Check both tangent’s own domain and zeros of the denominator.
steps: Tangent is undefined when cosx=0: x=π/2+kπ.
On the remaining domain the denominator is zero when sinx=0: x=kπ; cosx=1 is already included.
The union is every multiple of π/2.

problems.title: Two branches collapse into one family
problems.question: Solve cos3x=cos5x.
problems.idea: Equal cosines have equal or opposite arguments modulo 2π.
steps: The first gives x=kπ after renaming the integer.
The second gives x=kπ/4.
The first family is contained in the second.

problems.title: Count roots after sum to product
problems.question: How many solutions does 2sin((x+3)/2)=sinx+sin3 have on [-2π,2π]?
problems.idea: Factor using the sine sum identity.
steps: The first factor gives x=2πk-3, producing -3 and 2π-3 in the interval.
The second gives x=3+4πk, producing only 3. The three values are distinct.

problems.title: An obtuse angle from three smaller angles
problems.question: M is on the perpendicular leg AB of a right trapezoid, MB=3,BC=1, and ∠AMD=2∠BMC. Find tan∠CMD.
problems.idea: Let t=∠BMC.
steps: The straight angle AMB gives ∠CMD=180°-3t.
Therefore tan∠CMD=-13/9.

problems.title: A section plane’s normal gives its angle
problems.question: In a cube, M,N,K are midpoints of BB₁,AD,DC. Find the cosine of the angle between plane MNK and base ABCD.
problems.idea: Use unit-cube coordinates.
steps: For example (K-N)×(M-N) is proportional to (1,-1,-3).
The base normal is (0,0,1).
The acute plane-angle cosine is 3/√(1+1+9)=3/√11.

problems.title: Read the net dimensions before finding volume
problems.question: A rectangular-box net has a side strip 20 m long and 4 m high; its full height including the two attached base faces is 6 m. Find the volume.
problems.idea: The strip length is the base perimeter.
steps: The attached base width is a=(6-4)/2=1 m.
Then b=10-1=9 m and h=4 m.
Thus V=1·9·4=36 m³.
problems.note: The dimensions are read from the scanned net; the extracted text omits the 20 m strip length.

problems.title: A right prism with a rhombus base
problems.question: All edges of a right quadrilateral prism are equal, and its two space-diagonal lengths are 5,7 cm. Find the edge.
problems.idea: The base is a rhombus and its diagonals satisfy a square-sum identity.
formulas: If edge=s and base diagonals=p,q: p²+q²=4s²; 5²=p²+s²; 7²=q²+s².
steps: Adding the two spatial equations gives 74=p²+q²+2s²=6s².
Thus s²=37/3 and s=√111/3.

problems.title: Product to sum cancels the common term
problems.question: Solve cosx cos3x=cos5x cos7x.
problems.idea: Expand both products.
steps: Cancel cos2x to get cos4x=cos12x.
The two branches give x=kπ/4 or x=kπ/8.
The latter includes the former.

problems.title: Remove absolute values using trig bounds
problems.question: Find the greatest value of |cosx-1|+|-1-sinx|.
problems.idea: Both signs are known because sine and cosine lie in [-1,1].
steps: The sine term is at most 1.
The maximum is 2+√2, attained when x-π/4=π/2+2πk.

problems.title: Add three face-diagonal squares
problems.question: A rectangular box has its three distinct face diagonals 5,6,7 cm. Find its space diagonal.
problems.idea: Each edge square occurs twice in the sum.
steps: The positive diagonal length is √55.

problems.title: Domain of inverse sine
problems.question: For which a is arcsin(2a-1) defined?
problems.idea: Its argument must lie from -1 to 1.
steps: Add 1 and divide by 2.

problems.title: Pair the two convenient sines
problems.question: Evaluate (sin10°+sin20°+sin40°)/cos35°.
problems.idea: The last two sine terms sum to cos10°.
steps: Replace sin20°+sin40° by cos10°.
Then the numerator is √2cos35°, which cancels the nonzero denominator.
